implementation_notes: The document is the source of truth and versioning is explicit per surface: a new path prefix or media type for a breaking change, additive optional properties inside the current version. Choose it when consumers are polyglot and the shape of HTTP matters (caching, status codes, content negotiation).
pitfalls: Hand-editing the document without regenerating types breaks the compiler-enforced link between contract and handlers.
Query/path parameter schemas are as much part of the contract as the body; untyped params are the usual place where the document and the handler diverge.

variants.name: GraphQL SDL schema as the published contract (resolvers as the translator)
variants.implementation_notes: The SDL schema is the published language and the versioning model is additive-only: fields and types are added, existing ones are never removed or retyped, and retirement is announced with @deprecated before removal, so there is no URL version and no /v2. The translator is the resolver layer mapping domain objects to the schema types. Choose it when consumers need to select their own fields and a single endpoint fits the interaction better than resource-shaped HTTP.
pitfalls: @deprecated is documentation only - nothing stops a breaking schema change from shipping, so schema checks against the deployed schema are required.
Field-level resolvers make it easy to expose internal fields as new schema fields without an explicit publication decision.
